record.scope: One run of the automated rehearsal of the first demonstration (scripts/rehearsal, step list version 6) against main in the real application: a production build in headless Chrome over the DevTools protocol, one page per session, a fresh synthetic workspace on acceptance slot 3, and the hosted models through the product's configured client, with main's production derivative worker and its depth model, and the host playing the run's workspace at its shipped pace. The living world runs in the starter: the first-use card's small square placed and taken back, the Create panel's square, inhabitants brought in, the world played and watched walking, an inhabitant inspected, someone using the square, and a pause. The person's path runs from uploading synthetic photographs in the drawer through their admission, model rights and review to the depth pass and scene grouping, a world made from them, the Companion asked inside it, and the return to it, where one more photograph is added to the made world on a confirmed preview. The human review is the rehearsal driver's stand-in for a person's review, stated in stand_in_disclosure; no person reviewed these photographs. Each step is a person's action with its declared observable results; each gate of docs/product-direction.md is reported with its first failed step, and a gate that rests on the stand-in never as a plain pass.

steps.reason: What this rehearsal runs, and what it cannot. It runs main's production derivative worker with its depth model (runtime.derivative_worker: MoGe-2 on this machine's CPU), which makes a point map of each reviewed photograph, and the scene grouping that closes each job; wait-for-depth-and-grouping observes both, and a made world draws each photograph from its point map. It does not run multi-view reconstruction. Scene grouping selects a group for pose recovery only when it holds at least three photographs, each with a point map (SceneGroupPosePolicy in exulanica/ingest/scene_selection.py), and the rehearsal's drawings are a day apart, so each is its own group and no scene job exists. The scene worker (exulanica-scene-worker) also requires the pose runtime image by digest as provenance (exulanica/ingest/scene_worker_command.py), and this machine builds no image, so it cannot be started here with a truthful record; Gaussian training needs GPU compute this machine does not have. No control in the application shows a scene's coverage.
A person's use of the experience and the demonstration footage are observed and recorded by a person; this rehearsal keeps a screenshot of each step as its own record.

what_this_does_not_show: The human review of every photograph was recorded by the rehearsal driver through the drawer's own controls as a stand-in for a person's review; no person inspected these photographs, and every gate resting on it reports passed_on_stand_in or worse, never a plain pass.
The photographs are synthetic drawings in a synthetic workspace; no personal photograph is involved.

The depth pass ran MoGe-2 on this machine's CPU in main's production derivative worker. No multi-view reconstruction ran: no scene group held three photographs, and the scene worker was not started (reconstruct-scene-geometry states why).
The proposed place was confirmed through the identity routes rather than in the application.
Stopping a right in the drawer was not exercised by this run.
One run: the Companion's answers vary between runs.
Access used the production build's operator token gate; account sign-in was not exercised.
No person observed the run and no demonstration footage was recorded; no frame time was judged. The walking measure counts the frames in which drawn walkers moved, over one window of one run.

The living world was watched in the starter at the host's shipped pace with one population of eight; the walking threshold comes from lane W2's two measured arms, not from a pre-registered held-out set.
Other work loaded the machine during the run (machine_load, from the GPU slot's own log lines); the times are not timing measurements.
